Striders Impex Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value of Rs 60 per share, offering a margin of safety of 17.2% [E30, E31]. The company demonstrates superior capital efficiency, with an ROE of 16.3% and an ROCE of 16.77%, both of which substantially outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E13]. This operational strength is supported by a conservative financial structure, evidenced by a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x and a successful reduction in total borrowings from Rs 20.79 Cr to Rs 13.38 Cr [E22, E24, E35]. Furthermore, the stock is priced attractively relative to its peers, trading at a P/E of 21.1x compared to the sector benchmark of 24.6x [E6]. While the company has achieved impressive compounded sales growth of 42%, the market has yet to fully reflect this momentum, as the stock sits at only 11% of its 52-week range [E5, E14]. Conceded: the company faces challenges regarding negative operating cash flow, high debtor days, and recent institutional outflows [E19, E20, E27, E28, E37]. Despite these headwinds, the current valuation implies an earnings growth rate of only 7.3%, which is well below the 10% base case assumption, suggesting the market is overly pessimistic [E32].

The bull’s reliance on a 17.2% margin of safety [E31] ignores the severe deterioration in liquidity, as the company reported negative operating cash flow of Rs -11.39 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -12.49 Cr in March 2026 [E20, E21]. While the bull highlights sales growth, it fails to reconcile this with a compounded profit growth of -12% [E15] and inconsistent operating margins [E17, E18], suggesting that top-line expansion is failing to translate into bottom-line quality. Conceded: the company has reduced debt [E24, E35] and maintains a comfortable current ratio [E23]. However, this is overshadowed by the alarming increase in working capital days from 86.5 to 133 and high debtor days of 156 [E38, E37], which explains the negative cash conversion of -2.03x [E19]. The bull’s optimism regarding the stock’s position in its 52-week range [E5] is contradicted by the significant institutional exodus, as foreign and domestic holdings dropped by a combined 6.52 percentage points [E27, E28, E29]. Ultimately, the lack of dividend payouts [E4, E36] combined with negative cash generation makes the valuation metrics cited by the bull [E6, E30] appear disconnected from the company’s actual operational performance.
